question: Solve the differential equation $$(1+x^2)\frac{dy}{dx}+2xy=1$$ by reducing it to the standard form of a first order linear differential equation and applying the integrating factor method.
explanation:
Standard Form
Dividing throughout by $1+x^2$, $$\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{2x}{1+x^2}y=\frac{1}{1+x^2}.$$ This is of the standard form $$\frac{dy}{dx}+Py=Q,$$ where $$P=\frac{2x}{1+x^2},\qquad Q=\frac{1}{1+x^2}.$$

Integrating Factor
The integrating factor is $$\text{I.F.}=e^{\int Pdx}=e^{\int\frac{2x}{1+x^2}dx}=e^{\log(1+x^2)}=1+x^2.$$ Multiplying the standard equation by the integrating factor, $$\frac{d}{dx}\left[(1+x^2)y\right]=1.$$

Integration
Integrating with respect to $x$, $$(1+x^2)y=x+C.$$ Therefore, $$y=\frac{x+C}{1+x^2}.$$

Final Result
The required solution is $$y=\frac{x+C}{1+x^2}.$$
